newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - fuel, naphtha, CFDs up, mogas slip.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - fuel, naphtha, CFDs up, mogas slip.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Friday with fuel showing a gain for the third consecutive day, naphtha edging up, but gasoline slipping slightly. Brent CFDs were a couple of cents stronger.
Heavy fuel swaps gained $1/1.50 with June heard traded at $85.75.

Dealers said physical barges were done as high as $88. They said the bump higher in prices was supported by crude's screen strength, but owed more to short covering in a tighter market - cargoes have been fixed out of the region over the last few days.

Brent CFDs were narrowly stronger with June 9-13 valued around -46/47 cents under July Brent, with June 16-20 gaining to -40 cents under July. Further out CFDs gained by a few cents and a June 9-20 CFD was sold at July -40 cents.
Traders said paper crude appeared stronger while wet crude was still labouring under plentiful supplies. A dated Brent, 16-18 June, traded a cent lower at July -49 cents.
Gasoline swaps levels slipped by $1 a tonne on June swaps to about $202 while July held broadly steady at $194.50. Traders said physical arbing to the United States had become more difficult.
Gas oil crack spreads were steady with 4Q at $.70, 1Q98 at $4.65 and 2Q98 at $4.10.
